feedback.problem: The second-degree Taylor polynomial of a function $f(x)$ about $x=3$ is given by ${P}_{2}(x)=1+6(x-3)+18(x-3)^{2}.$ What is the value of ${f}^{″}(3)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
This is an expansion about the point $x=3,$ so the coefficient of the second-degree term is $\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(3).$ 

In the given equation, we see that the coefficient of the second-degree term is $18.$ So, we have

$$
\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(3)=18\,⟹\,{f}^{″}(3)=36.
$$
